Furthermore, we show a result which indicates that the decay rate $|z|^{-2}$ may be sharp and faster decay may imply uniqueness.
item.dc:creator: Shubham R. Jathar, Jesse Railo

item.title: Topological transcendence degree and the dimension problem for perfectoid spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.01418v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $K$ be a perfectoid field of characteristic $p$ with countable value group (for example, $K=\mathbb{C}_{p}^{\flat}$). We study Zariski-closed subsets \begin{equation*}Z\subseteq \mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}\end{equation*}of the $n$-dimensional perfectoid closed unit ball $\mathbb{B}_{K}^{n,\mathrm{perfd}}$ over $K$. We use an example of Gleason, and its generalization obtained in the authors' previous work, to show that two natural notions of dimension for such Zariski-closed subsets, the Krull dimension $\dim(Z)$ and Huber's iterated transcendence degree $\mathrm{dim.tr}(Z)$, do not coincide, and that the gap between them can be arbitrarily large.
item.dc:creator: Dimitri Dine, Jack J Garzella

item.title: An Odd-Arch Family of Perturbed Hofstadter Q-Recursions: Gaussian Profiles and Exact Frequency Laws
item.description: arXiv:2611.01453v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: For every integer $p\ge2$, we construct a globally well-defined positive odd sequence $Q_p$ satisfying, after an explicit finite initial block, $Q_p(n)=Q_p(n-Q_p(n-1))+Q_p(n-Q_p(n-2))-(-1)^n$. Its binary block words admit the exact factorization $U_{p,k}=(A_k\overline{A}_{k+1})^{p-1}A_{k+2}$, producing exactly $2p-1$ alternating signed arches per natural block. The elementary word heights converge uniformly to the Gaussian isoperimetric profile $\varphi\circ\Phi^{-1}$. For each fixed $p$, this yields an explicit dyadic limiting profile with $2p-1$ sign transitions and a sharp relative-error constant $\Lambda_p=b_p/2$, where $b_p$ is determined by $b_p((3p-1)/2+\Phi(-b_p))=\varphi(b_p)$. We determine all zeros and parity crossings in sufficiently large dyadic blocks. For $p\ge3$, there are exactly $2p-1$ transverse even-index zeros, whereas the three-arch case $p=2$ exhibits an alternating four/six-zero pattern. An ordered frequency factorization gives exact dyadic histograms, moments, total-variation distances, and extremal multiplicities. The limiting frequency generating function $z^3/(2-z)$ is universal, although the highest finite multiplicities depend on $p$. Finally, the summatory function has main terms $N^2/4+(N/2)\log_2N$, an explicit parameter-dependent log-periodic term of order $N$, and remainder $O_p(N/\sqrt{\log N})$.
item.dc:creator: Marco Mantovanelli

item.title: Infinite Generalized Sidon Sets with a Negative Answer to a Problem of Szemer\'edi
item.description: arXiv:2611.01871v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct infinite $B_h$ sets that repeatedly attain the density scale of finite $B_h$ sets. For every integer $h\geq2$ and every finite $B_h$ set $F$ of positive integers, we obtain an infinite $B_h$ set $A\supseteq F$ such that $$ \limsup_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)}{x^{1/h}}=\frac1h, \qquad \liminf_{x\to\infty}\frac{A(x)}{x^{1/h}}=0. $$ The key is to preserve density while preventing additive relations between successive blocks. A positional encoding of the finite-field moment curve has $q$ elements in an interval of length $O_h(q^h)$, while, for each $1\leq r<h$, sums arising from distinct $r$-element multisets are separated by more than $q$. This separation allows whole blocks to be appended to a prescribed finite set without a further dilation. In particular, our result gives a negative answer to a problem posed by Szemer\'edi \cite{szemeredi}.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang, Wenkai Yang

item.title: Convergence in law of the maximum of the Riemann zeta function on expanding intervals near the critical line
item.description: arXiv:2611.01905v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Let $T \to \infty$, let $\tau$ be uniformly distributed on $[T,2T]$, and let $\sigma = \sigma(T)$ be a deterministic real part approaching $1/2$ from the right. We establish the convergence in law of the recentered maximum of $\log|\zeta(\sigma + \mathrm{i}\tau + \mathrm{i} h)|$ over $I_{\theta} = \smash{[ - (\log T)^{\theta},(\log T)^{\theta}]}$, for every fixed $\theta > 0$. Under explicit conditions on the displacement $\sigma - 1/2$, the recentered maximum converges to a Gumbel distribution with scale parameter $1/(2\sqrt{1 + \theta})$. The recentering is an exact upper quantile of the one-point law of the associated Haar field $F_{h}^{\mathrm{H}} = \Re\sum_{p^{j}\leq X}U_{p}^{j}/(jp^{j(\sigma + \mathrm{i} h)})$, where the $U_{p}$ are independent and uniformly distributed on the complex unit circle. The positive constant in the limiting distribution is characterized by a Gaussian process describing the limiting microscopic increments of the Haar field around a high point. The result is established without the Riemann hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Fr\'ed\'eric Ouimet

item.title: The signed error-sum function of tent-map expansions
item.description: arXiv:2611.01955v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper, we study the signed error-sum function of tent map base series introduced by Dai and Tang in 2011. We show that the function is discontinuous at every dyadic rational in the open unit interval, although it was asserted to be continuous. We determine its values at these points and analyze its range, differentiability, and variation. We also obtain sharp covering estimates for its graph and calculate the Hausdorff, box-counting, and covering dimensions of the graph, which are $1$, $1$, and $0$, respectively. Moreover, we show that the signed error sum agrees with L\'evy's function away from dyadic rationals and that the unsigned error sum is the Takagi function.
item.dc:creator: Min Woong Ahn

item.title: On a hybrid trilinear Hilbert transform
item.description: arXiv:2611.02167v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In this paper we study the boundedness properties of a \emph{hybrid} trilinear Hilbert transform characterized by a \emph{dual regime} which simultaneously exhibits 1) \emph{resonant} (zero curvature) features, \emph{i.e.}, modulation invariance properties, and 2) \emph{non-resonant} (non-zero curvature) features. Specifically, given $a\in(0,\infty)\setminus \{1,2\}$ and $\vec{\lambda}:=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\lambda_3,\lambda_4)\in (\mathbb{R}\setminus\{0\})^4$ with $\lambda_1\neq \lambda_2$ and $\lambda_3\neq \lambda_4$, we provide wide-range $L^p$ bounds for the trilinear operator $$ HTHT^a_{\vec{\lambda}} (f_1,f_2,f_3)(x):= p.v. \int_{\mathbb R} f_1(x-\lambda_1 t)\,f_2(x-\lambda_2 t-\lambda_3 t^a)\,f_3(x-\lambda_4 t^a)\,\frac{dt}{t},\quad x \in \mathbb{R}\,.$$ By combining variable multiresolution, multiscale wave-packet analysis, and Rank II LGC method, our present work establishes a common framework where the diverse methodologies of all of the following naturally converge: i) the maximal truncated bilinear Hilbert transform, ii) the Biest operator, iii) the hybrid bilinear Hilbert-Carleson operator, and iv) the non-resonant (curved) trilinear Hilbert transform. Ultimately, this work reveals that the hybrid trilinear transform sits on a critical intermediate scale between the purely non-resonant case and the purely resonant regime -- the latter remaining a challenging, major (open) problem in harmonic analysis.
item.dc:creator: Cristina Benea, Fr\'ed\'eric Bernicot, Victor Lie

item.title: Multiplicity one for a linear spherical pair and its unitary analogue
item.description: arXiv:2611.02670v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove multiplicity one for a linear spherical pair associated with $\mathrm{GL}_4(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and its unitary similitude analogue associated with $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)\times\mathrm{GU}(1,1)(F)$. Both results hold for all irreducible admissible representations over non-Archimedean local fields of characteristic zero. Generalized Harish-Chandra descent reduces the proofs to the analysis of closed orbits and their normal representations. The unitary proof combines reductions to the linear case with a rational classification of closed orbits and a separate analysis of the remaining normal representations. We also establish multiplicity one for unitary Shalika periods of $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)$ with arbitrary irreducible admissible coefficients. A theta-period identity relates these periods to the unitary spherical pair. By varying the splitting character, we prove that every irreducible admissible representation of $\mathrm{GU}(2,2)(F)$ occurs as a quotient of a suitable big theta lift, allowing the multiplicity-one bound to pass to the Shalika periods. The linear argument also recovers Rallis's multiplicity-one theorem for twisted Jacquet modules of $\mathrm{GL}_4(F)$.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Ge

item.title: On some positivity properties of the Riemann $\Xi$ function
item.description: arXiv:2611.02944v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove strict log-concavity of the positive functions $\Theta$ and $\Lambda$ with one-sided and bilateral Laplace transforms $1/\xi(\tfrac12+\sqrt s)$ and $1/\Xi$, respectively, where $\Xi(z)=\xi(\tfrac12+iz)$. For either function, log-concavity is the P\'olya frequency property of order two (PF$_2$). Without assuming the Riemann hypothesis (RH), but using its published verification up to height about $3\cdot10^{12}$, we further prove that both densities are PF$_{k_*}$ for $k_*=1\,810\,540\,931\,075$. The proof views $\Theta$ as a small signed perturbation of a density that is PF of every order, with an error bound independent of the order, so the numerical check reduces to scalar inequalities. Since $\Lambda$ is a Gaussian mixture of $\Theta$, it inherits the same order. Conversely, a pole obstruction shows that if either density is PF$_k$, then every zeta zero lower than the $(k+2)$-nd lies on the critical line. Finally, we prove that if RH holds up to height $T>\tfrac12$, then $\Xi$ satisfies the generalized Laguerre inequalities $L_n[\Xi](x)\ge0$ of every order $n$ for $|x|\le T-\tfrac12$, extending the case $n=1$ of Csordas, Ruttan and Varga (1991).
item.dc:creator: Suvrit Sra

item.title: Geometrization of Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer and Vogan's conjecture on local Arthur packets
item.description: arXiv:2611.03342v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We give a geometric analogue of Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer for a general class of reductive groups over p-adic fields with cyclic component groups of trivial or prime order. We prove that this geometric transfer coincides with Kottwitz-Shelstad transfer, adapted to the language of disconnected groups, assuming the local Langlands correspondence satisfying certain desiderata, including the Kazhdan-Lusztig hypothesis for the ambient group and its endoscopic groups. As an application of this geometrization, we prove Vogan's conjecture on local Arthur packets over p-adic fields: for quasisplit classical groups and their pure inner forms, all local Arthur packets are ABV-packets, and the distributions attached to these ABV-packets of Arthur type satisfy Arthur's local conjectures on twisted endoscopic character relations. This demonstrates the following general principle: for any reductive group G over a local field, an Arthur packet should be defined as an ABV-packet of Arthur type, equipped with the endoscopic pairing calculated by traces of actions on vanishing cycles or microlocalizations.
item.dc:creator: Clifton Cunningham, Alexander Hazeltine, Baiying Liu, Chi-Heng Lo, Mishty Ray, Bin Xu, J\"org Sch\"urmann

item.title: Good rational functions up to degree six
item.description: arXiv:2611.03368v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Locally recoverable codes (LRCs) are fundamental to the architecture of modern distributed storage systems. The Tamo-Barg construction of optimal LRCs was revolutionized by the introduction of good polynomials, which group evaluation points into local recovery sets. However, polynomial constructions are constrained by their inherently large Galois groups, which limit the number of totally split rational places. Recent advances have generalized this paradigm to good rational functions, which leverage the geometry of the projective line to achieve minimal Galois groups and subsequently codes with greater length. In this paper, we complete the classification of good rational functions of degree up to $6$ in characteristic $2$. By embedding the problem into algebraic function field theory, we explicitly determine the minimal arithmetic and geometric Galois groups for these low degrees. Furthermore, we move beyond asymptotic Hasse-Weil estimates by proving that the exact number of totally split places over extension fields obeys a linear recurring sequence (LRS). This gives an efficient method for computing the exact lengths and dimensions of the corresponding optimal LRCs and, in many cases, yields parameters beyond those obtainable from good polynomials.
item.dc:creator: Anuvrat Jaindungarwal, Divyesh Vaghasiya

item.title: Six equations in search of a finite-fold-ness proof
item.description: arXiv:2303.02208v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: By following the same construction pattern which Martin Davis proposed in a 1968 paper of his, we have obtained six quaternary quartic Diophantine equations that candidate as `rule-them-all' equations: proving that one of them has only a finite number of integer solutions would suffice to ensure that each recursively enumerable set admits a finite-fold polynomial Diophantine representation.
item.dc:creator: Domenico Cantone, Luca Cuzziol, Eugenio G. Omodeo

item.title: On the Stieltjes Approximation Error to the Logarithmic Integral
item.description: arXiv:2406.12152v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the approximation errors \[ \varepsilon(x)=\operatorname{li}_{*}(x)-\operatorname{li}(x) \qquad\text{and}\qquad \varepsilon_{0}(x)=\operatorname{li}_{0}(x)-\operatorname{li}(x), \] arising from the classical Stieltjes--van Boven and pure Stieltjes asymptotic expansions of the logarithmic integral, respectively. Our analysis is based on the discrete values \(\varepsilon_k=\varepsilon(e^k)\) and their increments \(\Delta_{k+1}=\varepsilon_{k}-\varepsilon_{k+1}\), for which we derive new unconditional analytic bounds. Using precise integral representations of the increments and sharp upper and lower estimates for the associated kernel integrals, we obtain explicit bounds for \(\varepsilon_k\), valid for every integer \(k\geq 1\). These bounds yield corresponding estimates for \(\varepsilon(x)\) for all real \(x\geq e\). In particular, we prove that for every real $x \ge e$, \[\varepsilon(x) =\frac{1}{3} \sqrt{\frac{2\pi}{\log x}} + O\left(\frac{1}{\log x}\right), \qquad\qquad x \to \infty.\] We then use these results to demonstrate that for all real number $x \ge e$ \[|\varepsilon_{0}(x)| = \frac{\sqrt{2\pi}\left|\frac13-\alpha\right|}{\sqrt{\log x}} + O\left(\frac{1}{\log x}\right), \qquad\qquad x\to\infty\] where $n=\lfloor\log x\rfloor$ and $\alpha=\log x-n$. This provides an explicit asymptotic description of the absolute approximation error associated with the pure Stieltjes expansion, including its dependence on the fractional part of \(\log x\).
item.dc:creator: Jonatan Gomez

item.title: Igusa Stacks and the Cohomology of Shimura Varieties
item.description: arXiv:2408.01348v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct functorial Igusa stacks for all Hodge-type Shimura varieties, proving a conjecture of Scholze and extending earlier results of the fourth-named author for PEL-type Shimura varieties. Using the Igusa stack, we construct a sheaf on $\mathrm{Bun}_G$ that controls the cohomology of the corresponding Shimura variety. We use this sheaf and the spectral action of Fargues-Scholze to prove a compatibility between the cohomology of Shimura varieties of Hodge type and the semisimple local Langlands correspondence of Fargues-Scholze, generalizing the Eichler-Shimura relation of Blasius-Rogawski to arbitrary level at $p$. When the given Shimura variety is proper, we show moreover that the sheaf is perverse, which allows us to prove new torsion vanishing results for the cohomology of Shimura varieties.
item.dc:creator: Patrick Daniels, Pol van Hoften, Dongryul Kim, Mingjia Zhang

item.title: Automorphic form twisted Shintani zeta functions over number fields
item.description: arXiv:2410.11166v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Automorphic twists of Shintani zeta functions encode spectral information about binary cubic forms and the shapes of cubic rings. We study their adelic integrals over an arbitrary number field, allowing ramified data, nonspherical vectors, and arbitrary unitary central character. For cuspidal twists the zeta function is meromorphic on the whole plane and holomorphic for $\Re s>1/4$.
item.dc:creator: Eun Hye Lee, Ramin Takloo-Bighash

item.title: Rubik's as Galois': the inverse Galois problem for the Rubik's Cube group
item.description: arXiv:2411.11566v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the Rubik's cube group can be realized as a Galois group over the rationals.
item.dc:creator: M. Mereb, L. Vendramin

item.title: On curious properties of the general size-biased distribution
item.description: arXiv:2412.19347v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We offer further results on a general size-biased distribution related to the Riemann xi-function we presented in [9] using the work of Ferrar. Curious properties associated with its expected value are presented, which are related to special functional equations. We also relate our observations to some recent developments related to the Riemann hypothesis.
item.dc:creator: Alexander E. Patkowski

item.title: \'Etude statistique du facteur premier m\'edian, 1 : valeur moyenne
item.description: arXiv:2501.15947v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish an asymptotic formula for the mean value of the logarithm of the middle prime factor of an integer, defined with or without multiplicity, with a relative error of size a negative power of $\log x$, thus refining and generalising a recent result of McNew, Pollack, and Singha Roy.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Rotg\'e, G\'erald Tenenbaum

item.title: A Study of Fine Selmer Groups Over Function Fields via Greenberg Neighbourhoods
item.description: arXiv:2506.22002v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Greenberg examined the local behaviour of Iwasawa invariants as functions on the set $\mathscr{E}(F)$, the set of all $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions of a number field $F$. Kleine later extended these ideas to study the variation of Iwasawa invariants in the context of Selmer groups of abelian varieties across different $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions of $F$. Let $K$ be a global function field of characteristic $p$. In this article, we examine the relationship between the Iwasawa invariants of fine Selmer groups of an elliptic curve over $K$ as one varies over different $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions of $K$, using the methods developed by Kleine. We also study generalised Iwasawa invariants of the fine Selmer groups over a $\mathbb{Z}_p^2$-extension $\mathscr{L}/K$, adapting the techniques used by Kleine, Matar and Sujatha.
item.dc:creator: Sohan Ghosh

item.title: On Hypothesis H of Rudnick and Sarnak
item.description: arXiv:2507.20653v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove Hypothesis H in full generality for ${\rm GL}_n$ over any number field. This result is a consequence of our stronger effective bound on Euler products involving Rankin--Selberg coefficients at prime ideal powers. The proof rests on a new analytic method, which employs a power sieve over number fields and an iterative argument to bypass the functoriality barrier that had restricted prior results to $n\leq 4$. As applications, we unconditionally establish smoothed $m$-level correlations of zeros of automorphic $L$-functions for a restricted class of test functions, provide an explicit polynomial bound for the strong multiplicity one problem for coefficients, and resolve the Selberg orthogonality conjecture with stronger error terms.
item.dc:creator: Yujiao Jiang

item.title: Continuation of Dirichlet series I
item.description: arXiv:2510.06523v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study Dirichlet series arising as linear functionals on an inner product space of meromorphic functions and establish a relation between the discontinuities of the former on the boundary and the poles and zeros of the latter on the imaginary axis. As an example application of Delange's Tauberian theorem, it is shown that the conjectured asymptotic in the additive divisor problem follows conditionally on the non-vanishing of certain meromorphic functions on the imaginary axis.
item.dc:creator: Kevin Smith

item.title: On a bound of $p$-ranks of Iwasawa modules of $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions over a quartic CM-field
item.description: arXiv:2512.08278v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime number. If a number field $k$ has at least one complex place, there are infinitely many $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions over $k$, and some authors studied the behavior of Iwasawa invariants of these $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions. In particular, Fujii studied the case where $k$ is an imaginary quadratic field and obtained some results on the boundedness of Iwasawa $\lambda$-invariants in a certain infinite family of $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions. In the present article, we give analogous theorems in the case where $k$ is a quartic CM-field. One of our main theorems determines all the Iwasawa invariants, including the $\nu$-invariants, of a certain infinite family of $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions over a quartic CM-field.
item.dc:creator: Takuya Yanagisawa

item.title: On Diophantine exponents of lattices
item.description: arXiv:2512.24913v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We describe the spectrum of ordinary Diophantine exponents for $d$-dimensional lattices. The result reduces the problem to two-dimensional case and uses argument of metric theory.
item.dc:creator: Nikolay Moshchevitin

item.title: A note on toric periods in unramified families
item.description: arXiv:2601.09418v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $A$ be the algebra $\mathbf{C}[X_1^{\pm 1},X_2^{\pm 1}]$ and $Q(A)$ its quotient field. In this short article we exhibit the correct normalization for the toric period on the parabolically induced unramified family over $Q(A)$, so that it behaves optimally under restriction to the parabolically induced unramified family over $A$. Finally, we explicitly describe the structure of the $A$-module given by the image of this normalized period. These results answer questions raised by D. Prasad, and point towards potential generalizations to a broader unramified Gan-Gross-Prasad setting.
item.dc:creator: Alexandros Groutides

item.title: $p$-Ordinary Part of Hyperbolic Cycles on Modular Curves
item.description: arXiv:2603.21945v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this paper, we study hyperbolic cycles in the first homology group of congruence subgroups of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ with local coefficients. We prove that, for any prime number $p$, the $p$-ordinary part of the first homology group is generated by hyperbolic cycles.
item.dc:creator: Hohto Bekki, Ryotaro Sakamoto

item.title: Galois representation of the product of two Drinfeld modules of generic characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2603.27710v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the adelic Galois representations attached to products of two Drinfeld modules of generic characteristic. As a function-field analogue of Serre's open image theorem for products of elliptic curves, we show that the image of the joint adelic representation is commensurable with the subgroup defined by the natural determinant compatibility conditions if and only if at least one of the two Drinfeld modules has potential complex multiplication, or the two modules are not geometrically isogenous up to any Frobenius twist. Our proof combines Pink's theory of minimal quasi-models, explicit reciprocity laws from global class field theory, and an analysis of residual Galois representations. As an arithmetic application, we prove a torsion finiteness result: if one of the Drinfeld modules has no potential complex multiplication and the two are not geometrically isogenous up to any Frobenius twist, then that Drinfeld module has only finitely many torsion points over the compositum of the maximal abelian extension of the base field and the torsion field of the other module. This is an analogue of the classical results of Ribet and Zarhin for abelian varieties.
item.dc:creator: Lian Duan (with an appendix by Xuanyou Li), Jiangxue Fang (with an appendix by Xuanyou Li)

item.title: Minimal $a$-numbers of Artin--Schreier covers of ordinary curves
item.description: arXiv:2604.20091v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $k$ be a perfect field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $d$ be a positive integer not divisible by $p$. We define a non-empty Zariski open subset $U$ of the space of polynomials of degree $d$, and for $f(x)\in U(k)$, we compute the $a$-number of the curve defined by $y^p-y=f(x)$. This $a$-number realizes a lower bound given by Booher and Cais, so the latter is tight. Our result also implies that the bound of Booher and Cais for minimal $a$-numbers of Artin-Schreier covers of ordinary curves is tight.
item.dc:creator: Bryden Cais, Douglas Ulmer

item.title: Integer points close to a transcendental curve: an algorithmic approach
item.description: arXiv:2606.04858v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this article, we propose an algorithmic approach to determine the integer points located near a transcendental curve. This approach is closely related to a celebrated work by Bombieri and Pila and to the so-called Coppersmith's method. We establish the underlying theoretical foundations, prove the algorithms, study their complexity and present practical experiments; we also compare our approach with previously existing ones. From a practical point of view, we focus on an instance of our general problem, called the Table Maker's Dilemma, whose solving makes it possible to evaluate a given function with correct rounding. Our experiments show a significant speedup. In particular, our results show that the development of a correctly rounded mathematical library for the binary128 format is now possible at a much smaller cost than with previously existing approaches.
item.dc:creator: Nicolas Brisebarre, Guillaume Hanrot

item.title: Divided differences and complex variations of multiple zeta-star values
item.description: arXiv:2606.16627v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Motivated by the known derived set $[1,+\infty)$ of multiple zeta-star values, we study finite multiple star harmonic sums and their infinite-depth limits. Divided differences give a cube-integral representation of their holomorphic interpolation on $\mathrm{Re}(s)>0$, which agrees with the Kawashima functions after reversal of the index. The finite-depth interpolations converge locally uniformly in $s$ as the depth tends to infinity, uniformly over all positive integer index sequences on compact subsets. For real $s>1$, these limits define a bijection from the infinite positive integer indices onto $(1,s]$. For each admissible infinite index, they tend to the corresponding multiple zeta-star limit as $\mathrm{Re}(s)\to+\infty$ with bounded imaginary part. For $\mathrm{Re}(s)>1$, we prove strict separation of every ordered pair of finite indices and of every ordered pair of infinite indices: either the difference or the difference divided by $s$ has positive real part throughout this half-plane, with the choice fixed by the pair. In particular, both index maps are injective. The proof uses a summation principle for functions with positive real part, established through positive integral representations and explicit kernel estimates.
item.dc:creator: Jiangtao Li

item.title: On finiteness properties of the unramified Iwasawa module of a $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extension with restricted ramification
item.description: arXiv:2606.22324v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In the present article, we consider $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions defined by restrictions on ramification at $p$-adic primes. We study the finiteness, the existence of non-trivial finite submodules, and the triviality of the unramified Iwasawa modules of these $\mathbb{Z}_p$-extensions. In addition, we give a new sufficient condition for Greenberg's Generalized Conjecture with some non-trivial concrete examples.
item.dc:creator: Takuya Yanagisawa

item.title: Symmetric Spectral Reciprocity for $\mathrm{GL}(2)$ and Uniform Subconvexity
item.description: arXiv:2607.04476v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish an explicit symmetric spectral reciprocity formula for twisted fourth moments of $\mathrm{GL}_{2}$ $L$-functions over an arbitrary number field. A Rankin--Selberg kernel gives a new analytic regularization of the formal Petersson identity for products of Eisenstein series, based on the rank decomposition $4=2+2$. The formula preserves the nonnegativity of the amplified fourth-moment spectral side at general levels. We further identify a new \emph{square-level concentration phenomenon}: after amplification, the dominant off-diagonal contribution comes from representations whose conductor is the square of a product of two distinct primes. Using square-level local test functions in the relative trace formula, we prove new hybrid subconvexity bounds for twisted $L$-functions. Combining these bounds with symmetric spectral reciprocity and amplification, we obtain the uniform estimate \begin{align*} L(1/2,\pi)\ll_{F,\varepsilon} C(\pi)^{\frac{1}{4}-\frac{1}{120}+\varepsilon} \end{align*} for every unitary cuspidal automorphic representation $\pi$ of $\mathrm{GL}_{2}/F$ with arbitrary central character. We also obtain stronger bounds for fixed central characters, a prime-level fifth-moment estimate, and applications to Rankin--Selberg and ring class $L$-functions.
item.dc:creator: Liyang Yang

item.title: The Siegel-Weil formula in geometry and arithmetic
item.description: arXiv:2607.06285v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The present paper is an extended version of the lecture notes of a course given by the first author at the summer school on Formulas of Siegel and Weil (Bielefeld, September 2025). We survey three perspectives on the Siegel-Weil formula: classical, geometric, and arithmetic. We first recall the Siegel-Weil formula for elliptic theta series arising from positive definite lattices. We next discuss the higher genus case for lattices of arbitrary signature from an adelic viewpoint. After introducing orthogonal Shimura varieties, we present the geometric Siegel-Weil formula, in which the generating series of volumes of special cycles is shown to be an Eisenstein series. We conclude with the (partly conjectural) arithmetic Siegel-Weil formula, relating degrees of special cycles in arithmetic Chow groups to central derivatives of Eisenstein series.
item.dc:creator: Jan Hendrik Bruinier, Riccardo Zuffetti

item.title: Densities of arithmetic Hecke triangle group orbits
item.description: arXiv:2607.22142v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We give new proofs computing the asymptotic densities for orbits of the arithmetic Hecke triangle groups $\Gamma_q$ when $q=4$ and $q=6$. We use elementary number theory techniques along with basic properties of the M\"obius function and Riemann zeta function with additional congruence conditions. This note actually came about by observing that, in the $q=4$ case, the underlying congruence condition partitions the set of coprime integer pairs into three classes of equal density.
item.dc:creator: Samantha Fairchild, Christopher R. H. Hanusa

item.title: Density of the multidimensional Lagrange spectrum
item.description: arXiv:2608.30735v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Lagrange spectrum is a classical object in number theory, defined as the set of values of $\liminf_{q\to\infty} q\, \mathrm{dist}(q\alpha,\mathbb{Z})$ where $\alpha$ runs through irrational numbers. It has a complicated structure, with the discrete part, Hall's ray, and a transitional part in between. One can similarly define Lagrange spectrum in the multidimensional set-up, and until now not much has been understood about it. In this paper we prove that, unlike in the one-dimensional case, the closure of the multidimensional Lagrange spectrum is equal to the interval between $0$ and its supremum. The proof relies on a correspondence between Diophantine approximation and dynamics on the space of unimodular lattices and proceeds by studying a dynamical counterpart of the Lagrange spectrum that we call dynamical Lagrange spectrum. The latter is shown to be equal to the interval between $0$ and its maximum by means of an argument utilizing the higher rank nature of the set-up. A passage from full dynamical spectrum to the density of the Diophantine spectrum is achieved by applying equidistribution of expanding translates of horospheres in the space of lattices.
item.dc:creator: Dmitry Kleinbock

item.title: On multiply induced characters
item.description: arXiv:2609.04764v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate finite group structures that yield complex irreducible characters induced simultaneously from two or more distinct subgroups. When such a group is realized as the Galois group of a Galois extension of number fields, this phenomenon implies that multiple subfields share the same Artin $L$-function.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: Journal of Pure and Applied Algebra, 2026, Article 108430
item.dc:creator: Masanari Kida, Kyohei Matsukawa, Hikari Watanabe

item.title: Mahler's Problem on Liouville Numbers I. Analytic Rigidity
item.description: arXiv:2609.14202v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In 1984, Mahler asked whether a transcendental entire function can map the set of Liouville numbers $\mathscr{L}$ into itself. We answer this question in the negative by proving a local rigidity theorem for real-analytic functions. More precisely, if $U\subset\mathbb{R}$ is an open interval and $f:U\to\mathbb{R}$ is real-analytic with $f(\mathscr{L}\cap U)\subseteq\mathscr{L}$, then $f$ is the restriction to $U$ of a rational function in $\mathbb{R}(x)$. Quantitatively, there exists an absolute constant $\tau>2$ such that, for every nonrational real-analytic function $f$ and every nonempty open subinterval $V\subset U$, the set of $\xi\in V\cap\mathscr{L}$ satisfying $\mu(f(\xi))\leq\tau$ contains a Cantor set. The proof combines a two-height counting estimate near analytic graphs with a nested-interval construction.
item.dc:creator: Diego Marques

item.title: Surjectivity of the Enots Wolley Sequence
item.description: arXiv:2609.18054v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that the Enots-Wolley sequence, a greedy sequence defined by local divisibility and coprimality conditions, contains every positive integer with at least two distinct prime divisors. This resolves an open conjecture by Shannon and Sloane. The only analytic number-theoretic inputs are the prime number theorem and Mertens' estimate for reciprocal primes.
item.dc:creator: Nathan Myles Nichols

item.title: A new family of maximal curves not covered by the Hermitian curve
item.description: arXiv:2609.19546v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For every prime power $q$ and integer $n\ge1$, we give a single Kummer equation defining an $\mathbb{F}_{q^{2n}}$-maximal curve $\mathcal X_{q,n}$. The family recovers the Hermitian curves for $n=1,2$, the Giulietti--Korchm\'aros curve for $n=3$, and the Beelen--Montanucci curves for odd $n\ge5$. For $q>2$ and even $n\ge4$, it gives new maximal curves of genus $(q^2-1)q^n/2$ that are not covered by the Hermitian curve over $\mathbb{F}_{q^{2n}}$. We compute the genus for both parities of $n$ and give a uniform proof of maximality by counting rational places. For $q>2$ and odd $n\ge5$, we remove the Galois hypothesis from the known non-covering results for the Beelen--Montanucci and Garcia--G\"uneri--Stichtenoth curves. For even $n\ge4$, we determine the full automorphism group,of order $(q^n+1)q(q^2-1)$, and give explicit equations and genera for all Galois quotients, with closed-form equations for several classes of subgroups.
item.dc:creator: Liming Ma, Yipeng Wang

item.title: Infinitely Many Binomial Coefficients of Deficiency One
item.description: arXiv:2609.25042v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A binomial coefficient $\binom{n}{k}$ is good if all its prime divisors exceed $k$, and its deficiency is the number of $k$-smooth integers in $(n-k,n]$. A short constructive proof of the existence of infinitely many good binomial coefficients with deficiency exactly one is given, which provides an answer to a problem of Erd\H{o}s, Lacampagne, and Selfridge.
item.dc:creator: Xu Zhang

item.title: Strong Artin Conjecture for Generalized Octahedral Representations in $\mathrm{GL}_3$
item.description: arXiv:2609.38231v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove the strong Artin conjecture for the largest solvable Artin representations in three dimensions, whose projective image is isomorphic to the affine special linear group $C_3^2\rtimes \mathrm{SL}(2, 3)$. It is also the last solvable case in three dimensions. This is achieved with a new case of base change and automorphic induction for non-Galois quartic extensions with no intermediate fields. We additionally deduce the strong Artin conjecture for all 6-dimensional primitive solvable Artin representations.
item.dc:creator: Junwu Wang

item.title: Terminal Blocks of Primes in Pisot Numeration Systems
item.description: arXiv:2610.10026v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a prime number theorem for fixed terminal block words in a family of Pisot integer numeration systems defined by canonical block expansions. Suppose that the dominant root $\varphi$ is a Pisot number and that the characteristic polynomial $P_h$ is its minimal polynomial. Then every terminal block word of total digit-length $m$ occurs among the primes with asymptotic frequency $\varphi^{-m}$. The result recovers the known Zeckendorf and generalized Fibonacci cases and extends the terminal-prime problem to irreducible Pisot-unit systems without assuming that the recurrence coefficients are monotone, that the canonical expansions are greedy, or that the finiteness property (F) holds. Explicit non-$\beta$ families and Pisot units failing (F) illustrate this extension. The main structural ingredient is a canonical block language whose expansion of the companion substitution fixed word records the corresponding integer expansions in natural order. This connects terminal conditions with Rauzy cylinder windows and then with a linear orbit on a compact torus. The required multiplicity-one geometry follows from Barge's pure-discreteness theorem after reversal of the substitution words. The same toral model yields prime genericity for finite factors of the substitution fixed word, polynomial sampling laws, asymptotic independence from fixed congruence classes, fixed-shift correlation formulas, and M\"obius orthogonality. Combined with established prime theorems, it also gives a terminal refinement of Chebotarev and arithmetic progressions inside fixed terminal prime classes.
item.dc:creator: Sungkon Chang, Johann Verwee

item.title: Statistics of divisor functions over function fields
item.description: arXiv:2610.11240v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Extending recent works on the restricted divisor function over integers, we consider an analogue of this function over the function field. We provide some exact and asymptotic formulas related to this function.
item.dc:creator: Muhammad Afifurrahman

item.title: Reasonable bounds for Restricted Polynomial Progressions in $\mathbb F^n_p$
item.dc:creator: Alex Burgin, Anastasios Fragkos, David Kruzel, Michael Lacey, Amelia Stokolosa

item.title: Additive complements to the primes and large gaps between Romanoff numbers
item.description: arXiv:2610.14127v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every set $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ for which $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$ contains all sufficiently large integers satisfies $B(X)\gg\log X\log\log X$, where $B(X)=\#(\mathcal{B}\cap[0,X])$ and the implied constant is absolute. This proves a quantitative form of Ruzsa's Conjecture 2 and gives a negative answer to the $O(\log X)$ question in Erd\H{o}s Problem 32. The bound follows from a more general result: for an arbitrary set $\mathcal{B}\subseteq\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$ and sufficiently large $X$, we construct a block of $\lfloor c\log X\log\log X/(B(X)+1)\rfloor$ consecutive integers in $[X/2,X]$ outside $\mathbb{P}+\mathcal{B}$, provided this length is positive. As an application, we obtain $G_{\mathcal R}(X)\gg\log\log X$ for the longest block in $[1,X]$ containing no Romanoff number $p+2^n$, improving the bound $G_{\mathcal R}(X)\gg\log\log X/\log\log\log X$ of Kalmynin and Konyagin. The argument also applies to $p+a^n$ for every fixed integer $a\ge2$. The key step is a lemma on large shifts, proved using truncated products of divisor sums and the removal of auxiliary primes dividing differences of shifts.
item.dc:creator: Artyom Radomskii

item.title: CM fibers of Shimura parametrizations and thirteen proofs of the class number one theorem
item.description: arXiv:2610.16953v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We determine thirteen entirely CM identity fibers of Shimura parametrizations attached to elliptic curves of rank two and conductor below $2000$. Each yields a proof of the imaginary quadratic class number one theorem. The argument combines the Gross--Zagier formula with the Ribet--Takahashi degree comparison to show that the fiber is completely explained by known CM points.
item.dc:creator: Jingxuan Geng

item.title: From Inverse Vandermonde Matrices to the Shift Structure of the Dirichlet Eta and Beta Functions
item.description: arXiv:2610.26408v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We investigate the asymptotic behavior of the inverse of Vandermonde matrices with nodes drawn from the quadratic sequences $u\_n = n^2$ and $u\_n = (n -1/2 )^2$. We derive new limiting formulas for the entries of the inverses, expressed through the even and odd central factorial numbers. These formulas are then used to study the asymptotic behavior of a ratio of determinants involving a modified Vandermonde matrix. For each node sequence, the corresponding determinant ratio converges uniformly on compact subsets of the complex plane to an explicit expression involving the Dirichlet eta or beta function. We then study a family of related functions and, using an inversion theorem, exhibit their shift structure: the shifted values of the eta and beta functions are recovered as finite linear combinations of the family, which yields an integral form of these values as integrals of polynomials related to the Bernoulli and Euler polynomials against generalized (half-)Clausen functions. A unified form of the shift representation, valid for an arbitrary base point z with Re(z) > 0, brings the eta and beta families under a single theorem. On the critical line the representation is unitary and the values on the two sides are complex conjugates.
item.dc:creator: Serge Iovleff (UR4662)

item.title: An Equivariant Main Conjecture for Branched $\mathbb Z_p$-Towers of Finite Graphs and Applications
item.description: arXiv:2610.27551v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $p$ be a prime and let $Y/X$ be a finite abelian branched cover of finite connected graphs. We consider a compatible branched $\mathbb Z_p$-tower above $Y$ whose total Galois group over $X$ is abelian. We construct an equivariant Picard Iwasawa module over the completed group ring of the total Galois group and give an explicit presentation of this module. On the analytic side, we construct an equivariant Artin--Ihara $L$-element at the top of the tower and isolate a modified factor whose value at $u=1$ is well defined. Our main result computes the Fitting ideal of the equivariant Picard Iwasawa module in terms of these special values and augmentation ideals determined by the inertia groups. As applications, we recover the main conjecture for branched $\mathbb Z_p$-towers from our earlier work and obtain finite-level Fitting-ideal and annihilation formulas which can be viewed as graph-theoretic analogues of the conjectures of Kurihara and Brumer--Stark.
item.dc:creator: Rusiru Gambheera

item.title: Statistics of entries of matrices from the general linear group over a finite field
item.description: arXiv:2610.29305v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ be the group of $n\times n$ invertible matrices over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$. How many matrices in $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$ are there with a subset of their entries prescribed? Motivated by the random matrix theory of classical compact groups, we address this question and various variants, with a focus on asymptotic results that are valid as $n$ tends to infinity. Our methods are Fourier-analytic, with the main input being an exponential sum over $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{F}_q)$, evaluated in 1955 by Hodges via elementary methods. Our results turn out to be related to investigations carried out in other fields, including coding theory, universality for $p$-adic matrices and algebraic combinatorics.
item.dc:creator: Ofir Gorodetsky

item.title: Admissible sets of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1
item.description: arXiv:2610.34556v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\mathcal O_K$ be the ring of integers of a number field $K$. A finite subset $\mathcal H=\{\eta_1,\ldots,\eta_k\}\subset\mathcal O_K$ is said to be \emph{admissible} if for every prime ideal $\mathfrak p$ in $\mathcal O_K$, the reductions of the $\eta_i$ modulo $\mathfrak p$ do not represent every residue class. The diameter of a finite subset $S$ of $\mathcal O_K$ is defined to be \[\mathrm{diam}(S):= \max_{\eta_i,\eta_j\in S:\eta_i\neq\eta_j}|\mathcal N(\eta_i-\eta_j)|\] where $\mathcal N$ denotes the norm down to the rational field. This paper computationally investigates admissible subsets of rings of integers in imaginary quadratic fields of class number 1 (such as the Gaussian integers or the Eisenstein integers) that are large relative to their diameter. The motivation is twofold. Firstly, there is the improvement of results analogous to the question of an upper bound for the least gap between large rational primes, which has been one of the great number theoretic successes of the twenty-first century. A second motivation is that there is the opportunity to disprove a variation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture. The calculations in the paper provide new records on the smallest distance between primes in the fields in question, and explicit counter-examples to a generalisation of the second Hardy-Littlewood conjecture in all bar one of the fields.
item.dc:creator: Daniel Shiu

item.title: Coprime matchings of divisor sets
item.description:
arXiv:2610.37512v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For a positive integer $n$, let $D(n)$ be its set of positive divisors and put $N:=	au(n)=|D(n)|$. We characterize the arithmetic progressions $\mathcal P$ of length $N$ that admit a bijection with $D(n)$ pairing relatively prime integers. Such a coprime matching exists if and only if, for every prime $p\mid n$, at most $N/(
u_p(n)+1)$ terms of $\mathcal P$ are divisible by $p$, where $
u_p(n)$ is the exponent of $p$ in $n$. Call $n$ an $M$-number if $p^p

We prove that $D(n)$ can be matched with every primitive arithmetic progression of length $N$, meaning one whose first term and common difference are coprime, if and only if $n$ is an $M$-number. This proves a conjecture of McNew and Pomerance. In particular, $n$ is matchable, meaning that $D(n)$ can be matched with the primitive progression $\{1,2,\ldots,N\}$, if and only if $\lfloor N/pfloor\le N/(
u_p(n)+1)$ for all $p\mid n$. We classify the matchable non-$M$-numbers, settle a conjectured divisor criterion, and prove that every divisor of a matchable integer is matchable. The proofs combine a Vandermonde determinant with a partition into shorter progressions. If $E(x)$ counts the matchable non-$M$-numbers up to $x$, then, as $x	o\infty$, $$ E(x)\sim rac{x}{\log x} \sum_{r\ge1} rac{(\log\log x)^{r-1}}{(r-1)!\,q_r^{q_r}}, $$ where $q_r$ is the least prime greater than $2^r$. item.dc:creator: Max A. Alekseyev, Basile Beyer de Ryke

item.title: Positive Values of Inhomogeneous Quadratic Forms of Type (1, 4): The Constant \Gamma_{1,4} = 8
item.description: arXiv:2610.41223v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let Q be a real indefinite quadratic form of type (1, 4) with determinant D \neq 0. We prove that for every c \in \mathbb{R}^5 there exists x \in \mathbb{Z}^5 such that 0 < Q(x + c) \le (8|D|)^{1/5}, and that the constant 8 is optimal. This establishes a conjecture of Bambah, Dumir and Hans-Gill and, together with earlier work, completes the determination of the sharp constants \Gamma_{r,s} for positive inhomogeneous values of nondegenerate indefinite quadratic forms. The proof combines classical reduction and gap theorems with uniform bounds for circular gaps of quadratic residues. A central step identifies the exceptional parameters in certain resonant reduced families: an explicit ladder of integer witnesses resolves their punctured neighbourhoods, leaving only three rational parameter points, subject to stated coefficient conditions. These are treated by retaining the coupling in a preceding, less reduced form. The remaining covering statements are verified by finite certificates in exact rational arithmetic.
item.dc:creator: Vineet Kahlon

item.title: Central values of additive twists of automorphic $L$-series
item.description: arXiv:2610.42008v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study series $L(x,s):=\sum_n \rho(n)e^{2\pi i n x}/n^s$, where $\rho(n)$ are Fourier coefficients of an automorphic form $\phi$ for a discrete cofinite subgroup $\Gamma\subset \mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ and $x\in\mathbb{R}$. Let $\mathfrak{b}\in\mathbb{R}\cup\{\infty\}$ represent a cusp of $\Gamma$. Ordering the orbit $\Gamma\mathfrak{b}$ by increasing denominators, we prove that the values $L(x,1/2)$ for $x\in\Gamma\mathfrak{b}$, suitably normalized, become equidistributed according to a standard complex Gaussian law, under natural assumptions on the Laplace eigenvalue of $\phi$. Previously this was known either when $\Gamma=\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{Z})$ or when $\phi$ is associated to a holomorphic cusp form. This applies in particular to central values at $s=1/2$ of additive twists of Maass form $L$-functions $\sum_{n\geq1}\lambda(n)e^{2\pi i n x}/n^s$, or to the Dirichlet-theta series $\sum_{n\geq1}\chi(n)e^{2\pi i n^2 x}/n^s$.
item.dc:creator: Sandro Bettin, Sary Drappeau, Jungwon Lee

item.title: Algebraically trivial automorphisms of irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2407.06007v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Given an irreducible holomorphic symplectic (IHS) manifold $X$, we call an automorphism $f$ of $X$ algebraically trivial if $f$ acts trivially on the N\'eron--Severi group of $X$. In this paper, we extend the approach of Brandhorst--Cattaneo to classify, by means of lattice data, all the pairs $(X, G)$, where $X$ is an IHS manifold of a known deformation type (to this date), and $G$ is a finite group consisting of algebraically trivial automorphisms of $X$ that are nonsymplectic. In particular, we classify even-order algebraically trivial nonsymplectic automorphisms, with or without trivial discriminant action. In the case of nontrivial discriminant actions, we show that such automorphisms only exist for finitely many deformation types and orders

item.title: Some applications of the Nygaard filtration and quasisyntomic descent in positive characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2507.08568v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This article gives an expository account of quasisyntomic descent and the Nygaard filtration in positive characteristic, complemented by several new applications to $p$-adic cohomology theories. The guiding result is a new approach to Illusie's comparison between fppf cohomology with $\mathbb{Z}_p(1)$ coefficients and the slope $1$ part of crystalline cohomology. We follow work of Bhatt-Lurie, but give a more elementary presentation which does not rely on the formalism of $\infty$-categories. We then revisit Ogus' comparison theorem between infinitesimal cohomology and \'etale cohomology, and give new proofs of several results on fppf cohomology that were previously obtained with the de Rham-Witt complex. We also determine the action of multiplication-by-$n$ on the fppf cohomology of an abelian variety, answering a question of A. Skorobogatov to the author. This is an expanded version of the author's master thesis.
item.dc:creator: Livia Grammatica

item.title: On F-pure thresholds and quasi-F-purity of hypersurfaces
item.description: arXiv:2509.06211v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that quasi-$F$-pure but not $F$-pure isolated quasi-homogeneous hypersurface singularities necessarily have $F$-pure threshold $1 - \frac{1}{p}$. This extends work of Bhatt and Singh beyond the Calabi-Yau case. We also classify the (quasi)-$F$-purity of Fermat hypersurfaces.
item.dc:creator: Jack J Garzella, Vignesh Jagathese

item.title: Generalized Howe curves of genus 4, 5, and 6 with completely decomposable Jacobians
item.description: arXiv:2604.18074v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Superspecial curves are important objects in number theory and algebraic geometry, and the existence of such a curve of genus $g \geq 4$ is an open problem, for general characteristics $p > 0$. As a computational approach to this problem, Kudo-Harashita-Howe (2020) showed that a superspecial curve of genus 4 exists in each characteristic $p$ with $7 < p < 20000$. Their method restricted attention to a specific class of curves, known as Howe curves, for which superspeciality is reduced to those of curves of genus at most 2. In this paper, we focus on a more specific class of curves, namely Howe curves whose Jacobians decompose into a product of four elliptic curves. By restricting our attention to such curves, the superspeciality reduces to the supersingularity of elliptic curves, which enables us to construct a superspecial curve of genus 4 more efficiently than Kudo-Harashita-Howe's method. As our first main result, we confirmed by computer the existence of such superspecial curves of genus 4 in characteristics $p$ with $20000 < p < 10^6$. Using a similar approach, we also propose constructions of superspecial curves of genera 5 and 6 from only supersingular elliptic curves. Furthermore, computational experiments establish the existence of superspecial curves of genus 5 (resp. genus 6) in characteristics $p$ with $13 < p < 10^5$ (resp. $7 < p < 10^5$).
item.dc:creator: Ryo Ohashi

item.title: Disproving Conjectures on the Davenport and Narkiewicz Constants
item.description: arXiv:2609.29878v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: The Davenport constant $\DD(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is a classical invariant arising from the arithmetic of ideal class groups of number fields. Closely related to the Davenport constant is the first Narkiewicz constant $\Nark_1(G)$, which arises in the quantitative study of algebraic integers and their factorizations. Gao and Geroldinger conjectured in 2006 that $\DD(G)\leq \sum_{i=1}^r n_i,$ while Narkiewicz and \'Sliwa conjectured in 1982 that $\Nark_1(G)=\sum_{i=1}^r n_i,$ where $n_1,\ldots,n_r$ are the invariant factors of $G$. Both are central conjectures concerning arithmetic invariants arising from the theory of number fields. In this paper, we disprove both conjectures. Moreover, we show that, for every fixed $r\geq5$, both $\DD(G)-\sum_{i=1}^r n_i$ and $\Nark_1(G)-\sum_{i=1}^r n_i$ are unbounded over finite abelian groups of rank $r$. We develop a probabilistic representation technique to establish a uniform upper bound for the Davenport constant: $$ \DD(G)\leq\frac{16}{5}\,\rr(G)\exp(G). $$ Our bound gives the first improvement of the classical van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk estimate: $\DD(G)\leq\exp(G) \left(1+\log\frac{|G|}{\exp(G)}\right) \leq\exp(G)\bigl(1+(\rr(G)-1)\log\exp(G)\bigr)$, by removing the logarithmic dependence on the exponent from this classical estimate, replacing it with the absolute constant $16/5$. Their bound stood unimproved since its establishment in 1969. The existence of $C=16/5$ also brings us closer to the most challenging conjecture on the Davenport constant, namely the Emde Boas--Kruyswijk Conjecture in 1969, which predicts that $\DD(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1.$ As a further application of our results, we disprove a conjecture of Girard in 2008 concerning cross numbers, an invariant with deep roots in the arithmetic of number fields and Krull monoids.
item.dc:creator: Guoqing Wang

item.title: $p$-adic spectral zeta functions via the inverse Stieltjes transform
item.description: arXiv:2609.33660v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Spectral zeta functions provide a standard tool for regularizing determinants of differential operators in quantum physics. In a previous paper (J. Math. Phys. 66: 083505, 2025), we introduced a $p$-adic spectral zeta function for discrete spectra via a locally analytic interpolation function. In this paper we extend the framework to continuous spectra using the inverse Stieltjes transform. Starting from the resolvent of a bounded operator, we construct a generalized distribution, called the $p$-adic spectral distribution, and define bosonic and fermionic zeta functions and functional determinants. We establish their analytic properties, special value formulas, and Stirling expansions, and show that our previous framework is embedded into the present one in the discrete case. In this approach, the bosonic and fermionic cases exhibit an interesting symmetry. As an application, we consider the position operator in $p$-adic quantum mechanics on an arbitrary compact subset of $\mathbb{C}_{p}$.
item.dc:creator: Su Hu, Min-Soo Kim

item.title: A quasipolynomial inverse theorem for the $\mathsf{U}^k(\mathbb{F}_p^n)$ norm in the high characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2609.33733v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove an inverse theorem for the Gowers uniformity norm $\mathsf{U}^k(\mathbb{F}_p^n)$ with quasipolynomial bounds in the case when $p \geq k$. The inverse theorem follows from a quasipolynomial structure theorem for Freiman multihomomorphisms, which are a natural generalization of Freiman homomorphisms to maps of several variables. The proof of the structure theorem for Freiman multihomomorphisms is the central result of the paper and rests on three main ingredients: algebraic regularity method, abstract Balog-Szemer\'edi-Gowers theorem and the theory of multilinear maps defined on multilinear varieties. The last ingredient originates from an earlier work of Gowers and the author, and is significantly expanded in this paper. In particular, once the theory of such maps is in place, the proof of the structure theorem for Freiman multihomomorphisms is relatively short, especially compared to the previous quantitative results in the inverse theory of Gowers norms.
item.dc:creator: Luka Mili\'cevi\'c

item.title: Hodge and Hodge-Witt polygons under specialization
item.description: arXiv:2610.05892v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We show that, in equal characteristic $p$, the Hodge-Witt polygon can only move down and domino numbers can only increase under specialization in smooth proper families. We also show that the Hodge polygon of the generic fiber of a proper smooth $p$-adic formal scheme over $\mathcal{O}_C$ lies on or above the Hodge-Witt polygon of its special fiber, where $C$ is a complete algebraically closed extension of $\mathbb{Q}_p$. We further show that, in this mixed-characteristic setting, if the crystalline cohomology of the special fiber is torsion-free in degrees $n$ and $n+1$, then the degree-$n$ Hodge polygon of the generic fiber lies on or below the abstract Hodge polygon of the special fiber. We illustrate these comparisons with explicit examples.
item.dc:creator: Yuan Yang

item.title: Making Every Number from 1 to N Under a Fixed Cycle of $+$, $\times$, $-$, $\div$
item.description: arXiv:2610.10095v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Start with the number $2$. At each move, combine two numbers already made, but the operations must be used in the fixed repeating order $+,\times,-,\div$. We ask for the fewest moves needed to make every integer from $1$ to $N$. Since $2$ is already one of the numbers we want and each move makes at most one new number, at least $N-1$ moves are needed. We show that $N-1$ moves are also enough for every $N\ge 9$. Conventional induction cannot work, because a division that comes right after a completed interval $\{1,\dots,P\}$ produces numbers already made. Instead we extend a completed interval $\{1,\dots,P\}$ to $\{1,\dots,3P\}$ all at once, which counting shows is the smallest multiplicative extension $P\to kP$ that can work, and then adjust the last few moves to reach every other $N$. For $9\le N\le 33$ we give explicit sequences, found by computer search.
item.dc:creator: Sean Lesmana, Theodore Tjugiarto

item.title: Campana strong approximation on generalized Markoff surfaces
item.description: arXiv:2610.13528v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For every smooth projective generalised Markoff surface $X_m$, every hyperplane section $H$, and every integer $n\ge2$, we establish Campana strong approximation with the Brauer--Manin obstruction for $\bigl(X_m,(1-1/n)H\bigr)$.
item.dc:creator: Dasheng Wei

item.title: Uniformly Bounded Orthonormal Bases of Homogeneous Polynomials on the Complex Sphere
item.description: arXiv:2610.14160v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We resolve the long-standing problem of Rudin concerning uniformly bounded orthonormal bases of homogeneous polynomials on complex unit spheres. Specifically, we show that for every $K \geq 2$ and $N \geq 0$ there exists a basis of degree $N$ homogeneous polynomials in $\mathbb{C}^K$ that is orthonormal with respect to the surface measure of the unit sphere of $\mathbb{C}^K$ and uniformly bounded by a constant depending only on $K$ on the unit ball of $\mathbb{C}^K$. Bourgain resolved the case $K = 2$ in 1985 and the case $K = 3$ in 2016. No cases $K \geq 4$ were previously known.
item.dc:creator: Felipe Gon\c{c}alves, Jo\~ao P. Ferreira, Maksym Radziwi\l{}\l{}
